headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP-capable tooling create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict risks; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers; firecrawl exposes web-content scraping and MCP-compatible client support. That creates a plausible default bridge where scraped or file content can be fed into ECC as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so interaction risk is higher than low.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is copied into ECC prompts or files without provenance tagging, injection is possible.
IF ECC consumes scraped web text as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate raw scrape outputs from prompt inputs.
Add a provenance prefix to all firecrawl-derived text.
Disable automatic ingestion of scraped content into ECC.
Review any MCP bridge for instruction-like strings before execution.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filters between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches security findings, git history, documentation, and secrets-related config, while firecrawl handles web content, screenshots, and API keys. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive ECC material can be exposed to firecrawl’s broad network/API surface. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is an inferred but credible medium risk.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or synced workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF ECC files containing security findings or secrets are passed to firecrawl APIs, those contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep ECC and firecrawl in separate directories.
Do not send ECC secrets or findings to firecrawl.
Use redacted copies for any scraping workflow.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can write the filesystem and modify git state; firecrawl is an API client/CLI with broad network egress and MCP-compatible support. If both are pointed at the same repo or mutable workspace, they can overwrite each other’s outputs or race on shared artifacts. The profiles suggest overlap but not locking, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or output directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF firecrawl-generated artifacts are committed by ECC without coordination, git state conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes to shared repos.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Check git status before each commit.
requires-engineering: add file locks or an orchestrator-level mutex.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and act on code, docs, and security findings, while firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data. If ECC treats firecrawl output as authoritative, errors or poisoned content can cascade into commits or downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workflows, but verification steps could reduce it.
conditions: IF ECC uses firecrawl output as source material without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF ECC commits or edits based on scraped data, downstream work products may inherit firecrawl errors.
mitigations: Require a human review step before commits.
Cross-check scraped facts against a second source.
Mark firecrawl output as untrusted by default.
Limit ECC actions to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before write or commit actions.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session data, hooks, and security findings; firecrawl handles web content and API keys. The profiles do not show a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported. I cite both because the risk arises from combining their data classes, but the evidence is indirect.
conditions: IF regulated data is scraped by firecrawl and then stored in ECC session files, retention obligations may be implicated.
IF either agent is used on EU PII without a matching DPA/residency setup, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Set short retention for ECC session artifacts.
Document data-handling boundaries for both tools.
Delete temporary scrape outputs after use.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and DPA controls before production use.
